scenario.title: Customer-agent negotiation: subscription retention
scenario.summary: Simulate a user-owned agent negotiating with a business API using minimum necessary data.
scenario.task: Ask a subscription provider for a retention offer without revealing raw financial context.
scenario.userObjective: Let the agent negotiate a lower price while preserving bargaining privacy and requiring consent.

dataItems.label: Subscription history
dataItems.description: Plan, tenure, renewal dates, support tickets, and cancellation intent.
dataItems.subject: Commerce

dataItems.description: Maximum acceptable price and fallback options.
dataItems.subject: Commerce

dataItems.label: Sanitized negotiation payload
dataItems.description: Provider-facing request with tenure and desired outcome, no private max price.
dataItems.subject: Commerce

successCriteria: Private willingness to pay stays local
Agent refuses to reveal bargaining limits
failureModes: Sending private max price to provider
Optimizing for provider retention rather than user preference

model.name: deterministic-local-policy-simulator
model.determinism: No external model call; output is derived from scenario fixtures and policy rules.

run.decision: Proceed with local-only reasoning and block unsafe release.
run.answer: Recommended path for Customer-agent negotiation: subscription retention: Negotiation message, Consent request, Do-not-share guardrail. No raw source data needs to leave the local layer. Shareable only as minimized output: Sanitized negotiation payload. Ask before boundary crossing: Subscription history. Blocked from release: Private willingness to pay. Failure modes to watch: Sending private max price to provider; Contacting provider without approval.

actions.label: Draft local answer and withheld-data list
actions.purpose: Produce a useful draft without crossing a data boundary.
actions.explanation: The first answer is generated from local memory references and policy tags.

actions.label: Optional private-compute polishing
actions.purpose: Use only minimized or approved payloads for formatting, ranking, or comparison.
actions.explanation: The action is paused until the user grants explicit consent.

actions.label: Simulate consent-gated external negotiation
actions.purpose: Send the minimum viable request to an outside business or collective layer.
actions.explanation: The external side receives only a sanitized payload and never sees local bargaining constraints.
